conversations.title: Duplicate charges from Stripe webhook retries

messages.content: Our billing-api keeps charging some customers twice. I traced it to Stripe retrying failed webhooks — every retry re-runs the handler and processes the same payment event again. Right now roughly 3 customers a day get double-charged.

The handler isn't idempotent. Options: (1) use Stripe's idempotency keys on the charge call, (2) a processed_events table with a unique constraint on the Stripe event id, (3) make the handler side-effect-free and reconcile later.
Which is simplest to ship this week?

Option 2 — check the Stripe event id against processed_events inside the same Postgres transaction as the charge insert. Retries then become no-ops. You'll want a migration for the unique index and integration tests that replay the same event twice.

OK, going with the processed_events check. So today retries re-process payments and double-charge customers; after this change retries should be safely ignored. Draft the migration and the test plan for me.

conversations.title: Feed API p95 at 800ms — Redis cache or materialized view?

messages.content: The mobile-backend feed endpoint is slow — p95 latency is around 800ms. Profiling shows an N+1 pattern: every feed request re-joins activities, likes, and comments for the whole friend graph. What are my options?

Two realistic ones: (1) a Redis cache in front of the composed feed with a short TTL and write-through invalidation on new posts and comments, (2) a Postgres materialized view refreshed on a schedule. Given the bursty comment write pattern, option 1 gives better staleness behavior with less schema surgery.

60 seconds covers the hot path; invalidate explicitly on post and comment writes so authors see their own content immediately. Today every feed request recomputes the full join — with the cache, only the first request per minute pays that cost.
OK — Redis, 60s TTL, explicit invalidation on writes. Sketch the module boundaries and the load test we should run before shipping.

conversations.title: Friendlier way to decline a meeting invite

messages.content: Give me three friendlier rewordings of this Slack message: "Can't make the sync, send notes."

1) "Sadly I can't join the sync — could you share the notes afterwards?" 2) "I'll have to skip this one — mind forwarding the notes?" 3) "Can't make it this time, but I'd love to catch up on the notes!"

conversations.title: Migrating CI from CircleCI to GitHub Actions — strategy

messages.content: platform-infra pays about $1.9k/month for CircleCI across 18 jobs and the bill keeps climbing. I want to move to GitHub Actions. Cloud runners or self-hosted?

With your existing k8s cluster, self-hosted runners on spot nodes cost roughly a quarter of cloud runners at your job volume. The catch: runner registration tokens need infra approval, and you should migrate job-by-job while keeping CircleCI running in parallel.
Self-hosted it is. Today every CI run happens on CircleCI; the goal is all 18 jobs on GitHub Actions with the CircleCI project archived. Give me a migration order that keeps deploys safe.

Migrate lint, unit, and integration jobs first — cheap to verify — and leave the 6 deploy jobs for last since they need the runner tokens. Keep both CIs green on the same commit until the final cutover.
